nodes.summary: The decision problem SINGLE-MACHINE WEIGHTED COMPLETION WITH PRECEDENCE on bitstrings belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP reduces to it by a polynomial-time many-one reduction.
nodes.title: SINGLE-MACHINE WEIGHTED COMPLETION WITH PRECEDENCE is NP-complete

nodes.summary: Let $J$ be a list of jobs, each a pair (processing time, weight), let $(t, s)$ be a state consisting of the elapsed time $t$ and the accumulated weighted completion time $s$, and let $j$ be a job index. With $(p, w)$ the job at position $j$ of $J$ counting from $0$, or $(0, 0)$ if $J$ has no such position, the step sends $(t, s)$ to $(t + p, s + w (t + p))$.
nodes.title: One step of the weighted completion time computation

nodes.summary: Let $J$ be a list of jobs, each a pair $(p_i, w_i)$ of processing time and weight indexed from $0$, with $(p_i, w_i) = (0, 0)$ for $i$ outside the list. For a list $j_1, \dots, j_m$ of job indices, the total weighted completion time is $\sum_{k=1}^{m} w_{j_k} C_k$, where $C_k = p_{j_1} + \dots + p_{j_k}$ is the completion time of the $k$-th job in the order.
nodes.title: Total weighted completion time of a job order

nodes.summary: An instance $(J, P, K)$ whose job list $J$ has $n$ jobs is well formed when every precedence pair $(a, b)$ in $P$ satisfies $a < n$, $b < n$ and $a \ne b$.
